title: Core and valence photoemission spectra of atoms and molecules from a multichannel Dyson equation
authors: Stefano Paggi, J. Arjan Berger, Pina Romaniello
abstract: We recently presented multichannel Dyson equations for the \textit{ab initio} simulation of various spectroscopies. In particular, we introduced a multichannel Dyson equation for the description of photoemission spectra. In this work, we apply our approach to the simulation of photoemission spectra of atoms and molecules. We introduce a numerically efficient approach to calculate their spectral functions. We compare the spectra obtained within the multichannel Dyson equation to those obtained with full configuration interaction and the $GW$ method. We are thus able to show that the satellite features due to shake-up processes are significantly better described by the multichannel Dyson equation than by $GW$. Finally, we also discuss the slow convergence of the satellite energies with the size of the basis set and we propose a simple extrapolation method to reach the complete basis-set limit.
summary: This paper develops and applies a multichannel Dyson equation formalism to calculate core and valence photoemission spectra for atoms and molecules. It demonstrates that this method significantly improves the description of shake-up satellite features compared to standard GW calculations. The authors also address computational limitations by proposing an extrapolation scheme to estimate results in the complete basis set limit.
main_problem: The core problem is accurately simulating core and valence photoemission spectra of atoms and molecules by correctly accounting for strong electron correlation effects, especially shake-up satellite features.
main_result: The multichannel Dyson equation (MCDE) significantly outperforms the GW method in describing these crucial satellite features. The authors also propose an extrapolation technique to estimate results in the complete basis set limit.
method: The study employs a multichannel Dyson Equation approach, which is compared against benchmark calculations from Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) and the GW method.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to model photoemission spectra for various atoms and small molecules (e.g., Neon, H2O, NH3). The formalism involves coupling the 1-Green's Function to higher-order correlation channels.
key_observables: Photoemission spectral functions A(omega), quasi-particle energies, and satellite binding energies.
important_parameters: The convergence of satellite energies with respect to basis set size (requiring extrapolation) is a key parameter/regime discussed.
main_assumptions: Key approximations include the use of the (3,1)-MCDE formalism, which omits full screening effects in $\Sigma_{3p}$, leading to potential overestimation of satellite binding energies.
figures_summary: Figures compare spectral functions for several molecules across different basis sets, demonstrating the convergence behavior and comparing MCDE results against FCI/GW benchmarks.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the (3,1)-MCDE formalism, details its application to calculate spectral functions, compares these results rigorously with established methods like FCI and GW, and concludes by proposing extrapolation techniques for basis set convergence.
why_interesting: This work tackles a fundamental challenge in many-body physics—accurately capturing correlation effects beyond mean-field approximations—which is central to understanding excited states and spectroscopy in condensed matter and molecular systems.
